title: A Tragic Fire and Broken Promises in South Africa

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A devastating fire in Johannesburg last week is raising troubling questions about chaos and dysfunction in Africa's richest city.
sentences.zh: 上周约翰内斯堡发生的一场毁灭性火灾，引发了人们对这座非洲最富裕城市混乱与功能失调的担忧。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Lindsay Shuttel, on how the city that was once a symbol of the hope of post-apartheid South Africa is now an emblem of just how bad the breakdown has become.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事林赛·沙特尔将为我们讲述，曾经作为后种族隔离时代南非希望象征的这座城市，如今是如何沦为崩溃严重程度的缩影的。

sentences.en: It's Friday, September 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月8日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, Lindsay, tell me about the fire you've been reporting on in Johannesburg, which, as it turns out, is the deadliest residential fire in South African history.
sentences.zh: 那么，林赛，跟我聊聊你一直在报道的约翰内斯堡大火吧，事实证明，这是南非历史上最为惨烈的住宅火灾。

sentences.en: So last Thursday, at about one o'clock in the morning, smoke began to rise from this downtown building.
sentences.zh: 上周四凌晨一点左右，这座市中心的建筑开始冒烟。

sentences.en: And by the time I woke up...
sentences.zh: 等我醒来时……

sentences.en: Massive blaze in the Johannesburg CBD this morning.
sentences.zh: 今天早晨，约翰内斯堡市中心爆发了一场大火。

sentences.en: It is a very quickly developing story.
sentences.zh: 这是一起迅速发展的新闻。

sentences.en: It was all over the news.
sentences.zh: 各大媒体都在报道此事。

sentences.en: Firefighters rushed to the five-storey building.
sentences.zh: 消防员冲向这栋五层建筑。

sentences.en: Now they are still searching through the building for more victiMs.
sentences.zh: 目前他们仍在楼内搜寻更多遇难者。

sentences.en: And the death toll kept rising hour by hour.
sentences.zh: 死亡人数每小时都在上升。

sentences.en: When I first turned on the TV, it was about 20 people.
sentences.zh: 我刚打开电视时，大约是20人。

sentences.en: Then it was 40 people.
sentences.zh: 然后变成了40人。

sentences.en: Then it was 60 people.
sentences.zh: 接着是60人。

sentences.en: And then by the end of the day, it was 77 people.
sentences.zh: 到了那天结束时，死亡人数达到了77人。

sentences.en: And I'd rushed down to the site, and the bodies were laid out in the street.
sentences.zh: 我赶到了现场，尸体被摆在街道上。

sentences.en: You can literally see that the bodies have been covered with metal sheeting, with blankets.
sentences.zh: 你简直能看到尸体被金属板和毛毯盖着。

sentences.en: People who had run out of the building were sitting there in shock on the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 从大楼里跑出来的人们震惊地坐在人行道上。

sentences.en: And it was just a scene of such devastation.
sentences.zh: 那真是一片满目疮痍的景象。

sentences.en: This is the building itself.
sentences.zh: 这就是那栋建筑本身。

sentences.en: You can see that it's burned from the back.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到背面被烧毁了。

sentences.en: It's burned from the front.
sentences.zh: 正面也被烧毁了。

sentences.en: And up here, you can see some of the residents who were desperately trying to get out, had left a mattress there and were jumping from the top floors.
sentences.zh: 在上边，你能看到一些拼命想逃生的居民，在那里留下一张床垫，并从顶楼跳下。

sentences.en: Even though the fire had been brought under control by the morning, by the time the sun came up, there was still smoke coming from the building.
sentences.zh: 尽管火势在清晨得到了控制，但日出时分，大楼里依然有烟雾冒出。

sentences.en: And there were just crowds and crowds of people.
sentences.zh: 外面挤满了黑压压的人群。

sentences.en: And what we realized is that these weren't onlookers.
sentences.zh: 而我们意识到，这些并不是围观群众。

sentences.en: These were people who lived inside this building.
sentences.zh: 这些人正是住在该大楼内部的居民。

sentences.en: So up to about 600 people, possibly even more, just standing there their entire lives just in ruin and in embers, quite frankly.
sentences.zh: 大约有600人，甚至可能更多，就站在那里，坦白说，他们的一生就这样化为废墟和余烬。

sentences.en: As someone who's from Johannesburg, how did you understand what had happened?
sentences.zh: 作为一名土生土长的约翰内斯堡人，你是如何理解所发生的一切的？

sentences.en: What did it look like to you?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，这是一种什么情景？

sentences.en: It felt horribly inevitable.
sentences.zh: 感觉这简直是一种可怕的必然。

sentences.en: So we have had a series of disasters in Johannesburg.
sentences.zh: 约翰内斯堡已经发生了一系列灾难。

sentences.en: And we've kind of just quickly moved on from them.
sentences.zh: 而且我们似乎总是很快就把它们抛在脑后。

sentences.en: For example, a few weeks ago, a street quite literally exploded in downtown Johannesburg.
sentences.zh: 例如，几周前，约翰内斯堡市中心的一条街道竟然直接发生了爆炸。

sentences.en: Cars flew up into the air.
sentences.zh: 汽车被炸飞到空中。

sentences.en: And thank goodness, there were very few fatalities.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，人员伤亡很少。

sentences.en: And you would think that seeing a giant crack on a main road would shock people.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得，看到主干道上出现一条巨大的裂缝会让人震惊。

sentences.en: But it didn't.
sentences.zh: 但并没有。

sentences.en: By day two, people had returned to their homes.
sentences.zh: 到了第二天，人们就回到了家中。

sentences.en: They carried on.
sentences.zh: 生活继续。

sentences.en: They cordoned off the road.
sentences.zh: 他们封锁了那条道路。

sentences.en: And that tells you something about what Johannesburg is as a city.
sentences.zh: 这说明了约翰内斯堡作为一座城市的特质。

sentences.en: In the last few years, we've seen Johannesburg slowly decaying, becoming worse and worse every day.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，我们看到约翰内斯堡在慢慢衰落，情况一天比一天糟糕。

sentences.en: And for those of us, particularly South Africans, what we're wondering is if the economic capital of the most prosperous part of the country,
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些人，尤其是南非人来说，我们在想，如果这个国家最繁荣地区的经济首都——

sentences.en: which is one of the most advanced economies in Africa, if you can't keep that city running, what does the rest of this country look like?
sentences.zh: 这也是非洲最先进的经济体之一——如果你连这座城市都无法维持运转，这个国家的其他地方会变成什么样？

sentences.en: And what is the hope for the rest of the country, quite frankly?
sentences.zh: 坦白说，这个国家的其他地方还有什么希望？

sentences.en: Okay, so let's talk about that.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: How did Johannesburg get here?
sentences.zh: 约翰内斯堡是怎么变成这样的？

sentences.en: Walk me through it.
sentences.zh: 带我了解一下全过程。

sentences.en: Bring me back to those hopeful early days.
sentences.zh: 把我带回那些充满希望的早期日子。

sentences.en: So Johannesburg is a relatively young city.
sentences.zh: 约翰内斯堡是一座相对年轻的城市。

sentences.en: It was when gold was discovered here in 1886 that everybody rushed here.
sentences.zh: 1886年这里发现了黄金，所有人便蜂拥而至。

sentences.en: And everybody from Eastern Europe all the way to China came to find their lives here and to make their fortunes here.
sentences.zh: 从东欧一直到中国的每个人都来到这里寻找生活，创造财富。

sentences.en: It was an incredibly diverse city.
sentences.zh: 这是一座极其多元化的城市。

sentences.en: But ironically, it's also where apartheid began.
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，这也是种族隔离制度的发源地。

sentences.en: That is the system of segregation where black and white and all races were kept separately.
sentences.zh: 那是黑人、白人以及所有种族被分隔开来的隔离制度。

sentences.en: And this is where Nelson Mandela, the iconic freedom fighter, began this fight against apartheid.
sentences.zh: 这也是标志性的自由斗士纳尔逊·曼德拉开始反抗种族隔离的地方。

sentences.en: And this was with the sight of so much violence and political struggle and pain.
sentences.zh: 这里见证了如此多的暴力、政治斗争和痛苦。

sentences.en: It is my great pleasure to announce the President of the Republic of South Africa, Mr. Nelson Kholi Lhasa Mandela.
sentences.zh: 我非常荣幸地宣布南非共和国总统纳尔逊·霍利拉拉·曼德拉先生。
zh_words: 纳尔逊·霍利拉拉·曼德拉

sentences.en: Then came 1994.
sentences.zh: 然后迎来了1994年。

sentences.en: Out of the experience of an extraordinary human disaster that lasted too long, must be born a society of which all humanity will be proud.
sentences.zh: 经历了持续太久的非凡人类灾难之后，必须诞生一个让全人类都引以为傲的社会。

sentences.en: Apartheid ends and South Africa becomes a democracy.
sentences.zh: 种族隔离结束，南非成为民主国家。

sentences.en: Apartheid ends and Johannesburg sits at the center of that.
sentences.zh: 种族隔离结束，而约翰内斯堡处于这一进程的核心。

sentences.en: It's the crown jewel of what South Africa could be.
sentences.zh: 它是南非无限可能性的皇冠明珠。

sentences.en: Neighbourhoods are integrating.
sentences.zh: 社区正在走向融合。

sentences.en: Schools are integrating.
sentences.zh: 学校正在走向融合。

sentences.en: And for better or for worse, shopping malls are popping up all over during the early 90s, late 2000s.
sentences.zh: 不管好坏，在90年代初到2000年代末，购物中心如雨后春笋般在各地涌现。

sentences.en: They've got glass ceilings and cinemas.
sentences.zh: 它们有玻璃天花板和电影院。

sentences.en: The Big Mac has made it to South Africa.
sentences.zh: 巨无霸汉堡已经来到了南非。

sentences.en: And there's a McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 这里有了一家麦当劳。

sentences.en: The hamburger giant is planning to open another restaurant this month, then 15 more next year.
sentences.zh: 这家汉堡巨头计划本月再开一家餐厅，明年再开15家。

sentences.en: And in downtown Johannesburg at this time, even though white businesses and white families fled the inner city, feared in crime,
sentences.zh: 当时的约翰内斯堡市中心，尽管白人企业和白人家庭因对犯罪的恐惧而逃离内城，

sentences.en: they were replaced with migrants who came from all over the continent, from as far as Nigeria, Ethiopia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, would all come bringing their hopes to Johannesburg.
sentences.zh: 但取而代之的是来自非洲大陆各地的移民，远至尼日利亚、埃塞俄比亚、莫桑比克、津巴布韦，他们带着希望来到约翰内斯堡。

sentences.en: And so it becomes this multicultural, diverse, economic powerhouse that just draws people from everywhere.
sentences.zh: 于是这里变成了一个多元文化的、充满活力、吸引各方来客的经济发动机。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: The decision was taken after only one round of voting.
sentences.zh: 经过仅仅一轮投票就做出了决定。

sentences.en: The decision was made...
sentences.zh: 作出了决定……

sentences.en: FIFA announces that...
sentences.zh: 国际足联宣布……

sentences.en: The 2010 FIFA World Cup will be organised in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 2010年国际足联世界杯将在南非举办。

sentences.en: The first African World Cup will be held in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 第一届非洲世界杯将在南非举行。

sentences.en: It's uniting people.
sentences.zh: 这把人们凝聚在了一起。

sentences.en: It's everything.
sentences.zh: 这就是全部。

sentences.en: It's freedom.
sentences.zh: 这就是自由。

sentences.en: It's everything.
sentences.zh: 这就是一切。

sentences.en: I just love it.
sentences.zh: 我真是太喜欢了。

sentences.en: And there's a real sense of optimism.
sentences.zh: 这里弥漫着一种真正的乐观情绪。

sentences.en: Because here stadiums are going up, hotels are going up.
sentences.zh: 因为体育场在这里拔地而起，酒店也建了起来。

sentences.en: Very well down to South Africa.
sentences.zh: 南非干得太漂亮了。

sentences.en: I've never thought they could do it.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过他们能做到。

sentences.en: But they did it, man.
sentences.zh: 但他们做到了，老兄。

sentences.en: They did it.
sentences.zh: 他们做到了。

sentences.en: I feel it for them.
sentences.zh: 我为他们感到高兴。

sentences.en: And it's this beautiful moment of what South Africa could be.
sentences.zh: 这是南非可能呈现的美好时刻。

sentences.en: We feel safe on the trains and coming here.
sentences.zh: 我们坐火车和来这里时都感到很安全。

sentences.en: It's a good vibe at the moment.
sentences.zh: 目前的氛围很好。

sentences.en: And hopefully it can carry on after that.
sentences.zh: 希望这能在此后延续下去。

sentences.en: But beyond the World Cup, things began to fall apart.
sentences.zh: 但世界杯过后，情况开始急转直下。

sentences.en: And that's where the disappointment begins to set in.
sentences.zh: 失望情绪也正是从那时开始滋生。

sentences.en: So walk me through that.
sentences.zh: 那么带我了解一下那个过程。

sentences.en: What changed?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: So at this point, the party of Nelson Mandela, the African National Congress, is still in power.
sentences.zh: 当时，纳尔逊·曼德拉的政党非洲人国民大会仍在执政。

sentences.en: But we're beginning to see a different side of that party.
sentences.zh: 但我们开始看到该党的另一面。

sentences.en: This party that had these grand visions for South Africa becomes mired in corruption scandals from top to bottom.
sentences.zh: 这个曾对南非抱有宏伟愿景的政党，从上到下陷入了腐败丑闻的泥潭。

sentences.en: From the presidency all the way down to your local street councillor.
sentences.zh: 从总统府一直延伸到你家门口的街道议员。

sentences.en: But what that means is that the money that should have been spent on building schools, on paying for university tuition, on building hospitals, has disappeared.
sentences.zh: 这意味着本应用来建设学校、支付大学学费、修建医院的资金消失了。

sentences.en: Unemployment is rising.
sentences.zh: 失业率正在上升。

sentences.en: There's an economic crisis that is growing.
sentences.zh: 经济危机正在加剧。

sentences.en: And it turns into this sense of desperation that also drives violent crime in the city.
sentences.zh: 这演变成了一种绝望感，也助长了该市的暴力犯罪。

sentences.en: And perhaps the most material way South Africans are feeling it is that we literally find ourselves in the dark.
sentences.zh: 或许南非人感受最深刻、最实在的方式，就是我们真切地发现自己陷入了黑暗之中。

sentences.en: Around about 2012, 2013, rolling blackouts become worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 2012年、2013年前后，轮流拉闸限电的情况变得越来越严重。

sentences.en: And South Africans learn to live with the fact that the country is unable to supply electricity.
sentences.zh: 南非人不得不习惯国家无力供应电力这一事实。

sentences.en: And that is just one of the many things it was unable to supply.
sentences.zh: 而这只是它无力提供的众多服务之一。

sentences.en: And by 2019, particularly here in Johannesburg,
sentences.zh: 到了2019年，特别是在约翰内斯堡这里，

sentences.en: there was a backlash against the African National Congress when voters decided that they would not keep the ANC in power and voted them out.
sentences.zh: 选民们决定不再让非国大继续执政，通过投票将他们赶下了台，从而引发了针对非洲人国民大会的反弹。

sentences.en: What happened when they were voted out?
sentences.zh: 他们被投票赶下台后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Like, what did that mean for Johannesburg?
sentences.zh: 这对外约翰内斯堡意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, what that meant was political chaos.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着政治混乱。

sentences.en: So smaller parties suddenly became kingmakers.
sentences.zh: 于是较小的政党突然成为了左右局势的关键。

sentences.en: Parties that many South African voters had never even heard of.
sentences.zh: 许多南非选民甚至从未听说过的政党。

sentences.en: They were at the bottom of the ballot.
sentences.zh: 它们排在选票的最底部。

sentences.en: And suddenly they became the swing vote.
sentences.zh: 而它们突然成了摇摆票。

sentences.en: And these parties were then able to form coalition governments.
sentences.zh: 这些政党随后得以组建联合政府。

sentences.en: But those coalition governments were so rickety that Johannesburg has had six mayors in the last two years alone.
sentences.zh: 但这些联合政府如此摇摇欲坠，以至于仅在过去的两年里，约翰内斯堡就换了六位市长。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: A mayor for each season.
sentences.zh: 一个季节换一个市长。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I bet you if you asked any Joe Berger who the mayor is, they're not quite sure themselves.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，如果你问任何一个“约堡人”市长是谁，他们自己也说不准。

sentences.en: And so at this point, what that means is, who do you call when you're in trouble?
sentences.zh: 所以到了这个时候，这意味着当你遇到麻烦时，你该打电话给谁？

sentences.en: Who do you call when services aren't working?
sentences.zh: 当公共服务瘫痪时，你该打电话给谁？

sentences.en: A couple weeks ago, the copper cables on my street were stolen.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我这条街上的铜缆被偷了。

sentences.en: Copper cables have become a great underground business.
sentences.zh: 铜缆已经成了一门巨大的地下生意。

sentences.en: And so people rip out the copper wiring and it's sold as scrap metal.
sentences.zh: 因此人们拆下铜线当作废金属出售。

sentences.en: And that means that in your street, you will not have electricity, in my case, for up to a week.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在你的街道上，就我而言，会长达一周没有电。

sentences.en: Wait, the copper cable in your street was stolen?
sentences.zh: 等等，你这条街上的铜缆被偷了？

sentences.en: Like from city power lines?
sentences.zh: 就像从城市电力线上偷的？

sentences.en: From city power lines.
sentences.zh: 从城市电力线上偷的。

sentences.en: So what happens is, because we have these rolling blackouts, there is no electricity running through the copper cables.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的，因为我们有轮流限电，铜缆里没有电流通过。

sentences.en: And that is the perfect time to rip them out of the ground, to rip them out of power stations, and to sell them as scrap metal.
sentences.zh: 那是将其从地下扯出、从变电站拆下并作为废金属出售的最佳时机。

sentences.en: And it's not just the copper theft.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是偷铜。

sentences.en: It is the trash collection and the heaps of trash that are piling up around the city.
sentences.zh: 还有垃圾收集问题，城市四周堆积如山的垃圾。

sentences.en: There are these huge crater-sized potholes.
sentences.zh: 这里有巨大的、像陨石坑一样的坑洼。

sentences.en: And terrifyingly, in a city with high crime, the streetlights don't work in so many neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 更可怕的是，在一个犯罪率高的城市里，许多社区的路灯都不亮。

sentences.en: And that's what led me to start reporting on the decay of Johannesburg and just exactly what was happening.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我开始报道约翰内斯堡的衰败以及到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And back in May, my colleague Joao Silva, the photographer, and I actually end up at 80 Albert Street,
sentences.zh: 早在五月，我的同事、摄影师若昂·席尔瓦和我最终来到了阿尔伯特街80号，

sentences.en: which is the building that is now burned and become the center of such an awful tragedy.
sentences.zh: 也就是那栋如今被大火焚毁、并成为如此可怕悲剧中心的建筑。

sentences.en: And what I found was a hijacked building.
sentences.zh: 我发现的是一栋被劫持的建筑。

sentences.en: Okay, what exactly is a hijacked building?
sentences.zh: 好的，究竟什么是被劫持的建筑？

sentences.en: Like I think of a plane or a car when you use the word hijack.
sentences.zh: 当我听到“劫持”这个词时，我通常会想到飞机或汽车。

sentences.en: And that's nearly exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 情况几乎就是这样。

sentences.en: So what happens is, is that you have a building that is seen as vulnerable,
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，有一栋建筑被认为是不安全的，

sentences.en: a building where the landlord is missing, where it's clear that there's nobody taking care of this building.
sentences.zh: 房东不知所踪，显然没有任何人在维护这座建筑。

sentences.en: And so what you'll find is that groups of criminals or groups of gangs sometimes will walk into a building and start taking over rooMs.
sentences.zh: 于是你会发现，犯罪团伙或帮派有时会走进大楼，开始占领房间。

sentences.en: And they'll take over a room.
sentences.zh: 他们会占领一个房间。

sentences.en: They'll say, we live here now.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我们现在住在这里。

sentences.en: And under threat of violence, the people who do live there or people who want to move in, they start collecting rent.
sentences.zh: 在暴力的威胁下，真正住在那里的人或者想搬进来的人，开始向他们交租。

sentences.en: So the landlord is completely kicked out.
sentences.zh: 所以房东被完全赶了出去。

sentences.en: And people, criminals will collect rent for these buildings in which there's often no running water, no electricity, no fire escapes, no trash collection.
sentences.zh: 罪犯们会在这些通常没有自来水、没有电、没有消防逃生通道、没有垃圾清理的建筑里强收租金。

sentences.en: And the worst part is that there are dozens of them around the city.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是，全城这样的建筑有几十栋。

sentences.en: So it's almost as if these people, the hijackers, are kind of taking the building hostage, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎就像是这些人，也就是劫楼者，在把建筑当做人质，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they have seized it and they're extracting rent from people.
sentences.zh: 就像他们占领了建筑，并从中榨取租金一样。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: You can quite literally steal a building and have it function as a residential building
sentences.zh: 你真的可以偷走一栋楼，让它作为一个住宅楼运作，

sentences.en: without any oversight from the city and without any response from the city.
sentences.zh: 而没有任何来自市政府的监管，也没有任何来自市政府的应对措施。

sentences.en: Wow, that is wild.
sentences.zh: 哇，这太离谱了。

sentences.en: That is wild.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And what happens is that effect of the building that has been hijacked is that it affects the entire block.
sentences.zh: 而被强占的建筑所产生的影响是，它会波及整个街区。

sentences.en: And so the people who are living inside, because it's a mix of people, right?
sentences.zh: 住在里面的人，因为里面的人成分复杂，对吧？

sentences.en: But the easiest is for criminals to move into these buildings.
sentences.zh: 但最容易做的是让罪犯搬进这些建筑。

sentences.en: And so people walking past these buildings will often be mugged.
sentences.zh: 因此，路过这些建筑的人经常会被抢劫。

sentences.en: They will be shot.
sentences.zh: 他们会被枪击。

sentences.en: But there are also people who can't afford to live anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些人根本住不起其他地方。

sentences.en: And so they're living in these conditions as well.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也只能住在这样的条件里。

sentences.en: So it's a mix of the exploitation of Johannesburg's working poor, those people who came to Joburg to try and build a life and find that they can't even afford accommodation.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里既有对约堡城市贫民的剥削，也有那些来到约堡试图建立生活却发现连住房都租不起的人。

sentences.en: And how many of these buildings are there in Johannesburg?
sentences.zh: 约翰内斯堡到底有多少这样的建筑？

sentences.en: The number itself varies.
sentences.zh: 具体的数字各有不同。

sentences.en: The highest estimate is that it could be as many as 600.
sentences.zh: 最高的估计可能高达600栋。

sentences.en: But that includes empty lots and houses, because just as you can steal a building, you can also quite literally steal someone's house.
sentences.zh: 但这包括空地和房屋，因为正如你能偷走一栋楼一样，你也完全可以偷走某人的房子。

sentences.en: So what was this building like inside when you went in May?
sentences.zh: 那么你在五月份去的时候，这座建筑里面是什么样的？

sentences.en: So I will be completely honeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我实话实说。

sentences.en: I didn't go quite inside.
sentences.zh: 我没有真正走进里面。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: So the people living across the road warned us that we would absolutely be robbed if we went near this building.
sentences.zh: 街对面的人警告我们，如果我们靠近这栋建筑，绝对会被抢劫。

sentences.en: And so we watched people going in and out, and we saw this heap of trash right at the entrance.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看着人们进进出出，看到正门处有一堆垃圾。

sentences.en: We saw another heap of trash on the other side of the building sagging on the eaves.
sentences.zh: 我们看到建筑的另一侧还有一堆垃圾，堆到了屋檐下。

sentences.en: The windows were broken.
sentences.zh: 窗户都碎了。

sentences.en: It was pitch dark.
sentences.zh: 里面漆黑一片。

sentences.en: It was the middle of the day, but it was pitch dark inside the building because there was no light.
sentences.zh: 大白天里面却漆黑一片，因为里面没有光线。

sentences.en: And there were rats scurrying around.
sentences.zh: 而且老鼠到处乱窜。

sentences.en: And of course, my colleague, Joao Silva, who is a well-known war photographer, went back the next day because he was determined to take a look inside.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的同事若昂·席尔瓦（Joao Silva）是一位知名的战地摄影师，他第二天又回去了，因为他决心进去看一看。

sentences.en: And he got only as far as the lobby.
sentences.zh: 但他只走到了大堂。

sentences.en: If my colleague, Joao Silva, only went as far as the lobby,
sentences.zh: 如果我的同事若昂·席尔瓦只走到了大堂，

sentences.en: Joao Silva is one of the most fearless people.
sentences.zh: 若昂·席尔瓦是最无畏的人之一。

sentences.en: I know we were together in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我们曾一起在阿富汗共事。

sentences.en: It must have been pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 那里的情况肯定相当糟糕。

sentences.en: It was a case of he didn't know who was behind which door.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是他不知道每扇门后面藏着什么人。

sentences.en: And that's where the threat would be.
sentences.zh: 而危险就潜藏在那里。

sentences.en: So Joao walks around the lobby and he sees exposed wire.
sentences.zh: 所以若昂在大堂周围走动，看到裸露的电线。

sentences.en: He sees doors hanging off the hinges.
sentences.zh: 他看到门从合页上脱落。

sentences.en: And he just remarked over and over just how dark and unsafe the building itself was.
sentences.zh: 他只是一再感慨这座建筑本身有多么黑暗和不安全。

sentences.en: But in the aftermath of the fire, we've gotten a closer sense of what happened behind those closed doors where Joao wasn't able to go.
sentences.zh: 但在火灾发生后，我们对若昂无法进入的那些紧闭的门后发生了什么有了更清晰的了解。

sentences.en: Talking to the survivors, people who lived inside this building, and how they feared for their lives and how even they saw that this was an inevitability.
sentences.zh: 通过与幸存者、这座大楼的住户交谈，我们了解到他们是如何为生命感到恐惧，以及他们甚至如何看待这场灾难的必然性。

sentences.en: So, Lindsay, you finally find out what it's like to live in this building because you've talked to some of the people who live there.
sentences.zh: 那么，林赛，你终于知道了住在这栋楼里是什么感觉，因为你和一些住在那里的居民谈过。

sentences.en: What did they say?
sentences.zh: 他们说了什么？

sentences.en: So, the morning after the fire, I go to a community centre nearby that is housing many of the survivors.
sentences.zh: 火灾发生后的第二天早上，我去了附近一个收容了许多幸存者的社区中心。

sentences.en: And in one of the halls, women have been sleeping on donated mattresses with blankets.
sentences.zh: 在一个大厅里，女人们一直睡在捐赠的床垫和毯子上。

sentences.en: Can I come closer?
sentences.zh: 我能靠近一点吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: And on one of those rolled up mattresses, I find a young woman and her mother.
sentences.zh: 在一个卷起的床垫上，我找到了一个年轻女子和她的母亲。

sentences.en: Her mother's name is Pearl.
sentences.zh: 她母亲名叫珀尔（Pearl）。

sentences.en: She's in her early 50s.
sentences.zh: 她刚满五十岁出头。

sentences.en: It's like me and my mom.
sentences.zh: 就像我和我妈妈一样。

sentences.en: Just us.
sentences.zh: 只有我们俩。

sentences.en: And next to her is her daughter.
sentences.zh: 她旁边是她的女儿。

sentences.en: The building we used to live at them is another hijacked one.
sentences.zh: 我们以前住的那栋楼是另一栋被强占的建筑。

sentences.en: They had just moved from one hijacked building where it had become too unsafe for them because of the criminality in that building into this building here.
sentences.zh: 她们刚从另一栋被强占的建筑搬过来，因为那里由于犯罪活动变得对她们来说太不安全了，所以她们搬到了这栋楼。

sentences.en: And how long were you living in the building?
sentences.zh: 你们在这栋楼里住了多久？

sentences.en: This is the third one.
sentences.zh: 这是第三栋了。

sentences.en: They'd been there for a couple months, but they said that life was hell.
sentences.zh: 她们在那里住了几个月，但她们说生活简直是地狱。

sentences.en: It was bad.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It was bad.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It was bad to have been to a bike.
sentences.zh: 情况糟得难以置信。

sentences.en: Sometimes during the night, we'd have to wake up and lie on our stomachs because there were gunshots right in the passage.
sentences.zh: 有时在夜里，我们不得不醒来趴在肚子上，因为过道里就有枪声。

sentences.en: It was bad.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It was bad.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Sometimes at night, we'd hear ghosts screaming.
sentences.zh: 有时在夜里，我们会听到尖叫声。

sentences.en: And you guys were paying the rent for that?
sentences.zh: 你们还要为此付房租吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's the worst part.
sentences.zh: 这才是最糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They pay more than a thousand rand for this little corner of a room, which is about $50, just over.
sentences.zh: 她们为房间里这个小角落支付了一千多兰德的租金，大约是50美元，略多一点。

sentences.en: And they get this money from Pearl, who cleans the streets, and from her daughter's tuition fee that she gets from the state as a college student.
sentences.zh: 这笔钱来自靠清洁街道维生的珀尔，以及她女儿作为大学生从国家获得的助学金。

sentences.en: And they had no running water, and so would use water from the fire hydrant or collect water from an open drain.
sentences.zh: 他们没有自来水，所以只能用消防栓的水，或者从露天排水沟收集水。

sentences.en: Whenever you had to pee or relieve yourself, you had to go like four streets away, go to the council center.
sentences.zh: 每当你需要小便或解决内急时，你得走大概四条街去市政中心。

sentences.en: They had no toilets, and so they would walk up to the shopping mall two to three blocks up the road during the day.
sentences.zh: 他们没有厕所，所以白天会走到路上两三个街区外的购物中心。

sentences.en: And at night, when it became too unsafe, they would relieve themselves in buckets and keep it in the room.
sentences.zh: 到了晚上情况变得太不安全时，他们就在水桶里解决，然后把水桶留在房间里。

sentences.en: I had to be at home by five, as long as it's not dark yet.
sentences.zh: 我必须在五点前回家，只要天还没黑。

sentences.en: The daughter could not get into the building after dark, not because she was afraid of what was happening outside.
sentences.zh: 女儿天黑后无法进入大楼，不是因为她害怕外面发生的事情。

sentences.en: We'd have people rob you inside the building.
sentences.zh: 大楼里也会有人抢劫你。

sentences.en: But because of inside the building.
sentences.zh: 而是因为大楼内部的情况。

sentences.en: She would rush home and lock herself in the room before sunset.
sentences.zh: 她会在日落前赶回家把自己锁在房间里。

sentences.en: Because today I had no electricity, I was using wood inside the apartment.
sentences.zh: 因为今天没有电，我在公寓里用木柴。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The only way to keep the room warm is to make a small fire in the room.
sentences.zh: 保持房间温暖的唯一方法就是在房间里生个小火。

sentences.en: And they knew this was a fire hazard, and it was an awful choice that they had to make every day.
sentences.zh: 她们知道这是火灾隐患，这是她们每天都必须面对的糟糕选择。

sentences.en: So they knew that this building was going to be life-threatening.
sentences.zh: 所以她们知道这栋建筑会危及生命。

sentences.en: How did they describe the night of the fire?
sentences.zh: 她们是如何描述火灾当晚的情况的？

sentences.en: So on the night of the fire, the daughter had been studying late, and it was too unsafe to go home.
sentences.zh: 所以在火灾当晚，女儿学习到很晚，回家太不安全了。

sentences.en: So she stayed with a friend, and it was just her mom at home.
sentences.zh: 所以她和朋友呆在一起，家里只有她妈妈。

sentences.en: And her mom, Pearl, says, round about after 1 a.m., she'd gotten up and she wanted to relieve herself.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲珀尔说，大约在凌晨1点之后，她起床想去上厕所。

sentences.en: And she says, quite frankly, that something felt off.
sentences.zh: 她直言不讳地说，当时感觉有点不对劲。

sentences.en: So there was a sense of foreboding, and she began to pray.
sentences.zh: 有一种不祥的预感，于是她开始祈祷。

sentences.en: Then after I prayed, when I was about to go back to sleeping on my bed, I heard something like a sound of a gun outside.
sentences.zh: 祈祷后，当我正准备回床上睡觉时，我听到外面有类似枪声的声音。

sentences.en: And what she remembers thereafter is suddenly she heard screaming, and people were banging on the doors and saying, there's a fire, there's a fire in the building.
sentences.zh: 她此后记起的是，突然她听到尖叫声，有人在敲门并喊道，着火了，大楼里着火了。

sentences.en: And what it seemed is that in one of the shacks on the ground floor or in the lot outside, there seems to have been a fire.
sentences.zh: 似乎是一楼的棚屋之一或者外面空地上的棚屋发生了火灾。

sentences.en: And of course, we don't know exactly what the cause is just yet, but we do know that that fire spread rapidly because of the materials within this abandoned, stripped building.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们目前还不知道具体原因，但我们确实知道，由于这座被遗弃、被洗劫一空的建筑内部的材料，火势迅速蔓延。

sentences.en: Then I just took my clothes.
sentences.zh: 然后我只拿了我的衣服。

sentences.en: I took a bed.
sentences.zh: 我拿了一个床垫。

sentences.en: Then I walked out.
sentences.zh: 然后我走了出去。

sentences.en: I locked the bed like it.
sentences.zh: 我把门锁上了。

sentences.en: I was playing in my heart that way.
sentences.zh: 我心里当时就在那样祈祷。

sentences.en: May God just protect me.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑我。

sentences.en: Just show me the way.
sentences.zh: 请指引我出路。

sentences.en: Just safe.
sentences.zh: 只要安全就好。

sentences.en: Pearl says she got out of her room, but she locks the door because she's hoping that she's able to come back at some point.
sentences.zh: 珀尔说她走出了房间，但她把门锁上了，因为她希望有朝一日能回来。

sentences.en: And she grabs what she can.
sentences.zh: 她抓起能拿的东西。

sentences.en: She says she didn't have time to grab her door to school books.
sentences.zh: 她说她没有时间去拿学校的课本。

sentences.en: And she runs outside.
sentences.zh: 她跑到了外面。

sentences.en: And as she's running, she takes the risk of running down the stairs.
sentences.zh: 在她逃跑的时候，她冒着风险往楼梯下跑。

sentences.en: We know a lot of people were too afraid as the fire leapt up and they jumped out of the third floor.
sentences.zh: 我们知道很多人因为火势向上窜而感到极度恐惧，直接从三楼跳了下去。

sentences.en: Pearl is one of the lucky ones that made it down the stairs.
sentences.zh: 珀尔是跑下楼梯的幸运儿之一。

sentences.en: But she says on one of the floors, there was a locked door.
sentences.zh: 但她说在其中一层楼，有一扇锁着的门。

sentences.en: And she heard banging and banging.
sentences.zh: 她听到里面传来剧烈的砸门声。

sentences.en: And she says it is sound that she will never forget of a man screaming on the other side of a locked door.
sentences.zh: 她说那是她永远不会忘记的声音，一个男人在锁着的门后绝望尖叫。

sentences.en: And she had to make that choice.
sentences.zh: 她必须做出选择。

sentences.en: Does she go and try and free him?
sentences.zh: 她是要去试着解救他吗？

sentences.en: She doesn't have a key.
sentences.zh: 她没有钥匙。

sentences.en: I never, I never, I just thought of myself.
sentences.zh: 我没有，我没有，我只想着我自己。

sentences.en: I had to save myself because I know that I have a child to live.
sentences.zh: 我必须自救，因为我知道我还有一个孩子要养。

sentences.en: If I die, she will be left alone.
sentences.zh: 如果我死了，她就会孤苦伶仃。

sentences.en: It's what was running in my mind that, you know what, you cannot die in this fire.
sentences.zh: 我当时脑子里转的就是，你知道的，你不能死在这场大火里。

sentences.en: You have to save yourself for this child.
sentences.zh: 你必须为了这个孩子拯救自己。

sentences.en: It's the choice of, does she save herself for her daughter, who she lives for?
sentences.zh: 这就是她是否要为了她赖以生存的女儿而自救的选择。

sentences.en: Or does she run and try and save this man who she doesn't know?
sentences.zh: 还是她会跑开，试图去救这个她根本不认识的男人？

sentences.en: Because the truth is, she doesn't really know her neighbours.
sentences.zh: 因为事实是，她其实并不了解她的邻居。

sentences.en: And so many of the people, when I spoke to them outside, they said, we didn't really know who we were living next door to because people were in and out.
sentences.zh: 当我走到外面和许多人交谈时，他们说，我们其实根本不知道自己隔壁住的是谁，因为大家总是进进出出。

sentences.en: Then no one went there because we were running for our lives.
sentences.zh: 然后没人敢去那里，因为我们在拼命逃生。

sentences.en: We didn't know how far is the fire and what is going to happen, maybe the building is going to explode.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道火离多远，会发生什么，也许大楼会爆炸。

sentences.en: We just ran out.
sentences.zh: 我们只能跑出来。

sentences.en: She makes the choice and she runs in the opposite direction from the man who was screaming.
sentences.zh: 她做出了选择，她朝尖叫男人的相反方向跑去。

sentences.en: And when she finally makes it out into the street, she looks back and the building is aflame.
sentences.zh: 当她终于跑到街上时，她回过头，大楼已经陷入火海。

sentences.en: So I was standing there, some of the people were throwing themselves from the roof.
sentences.zh: 当时我正站在那儿，有些人从屋顶往下跳。

sentences.en: And people are jumping and some of them are falling to their deaths.
sentences.zh: 人们在跳楼，其中一些人活活摔死了。

sentences.en: And as she's saying this, she shakes her head and tears are just filling her eyes.
sentences.zh: 就在她这么说的时候，她摇了摇头，眼泪夺眶而出。

sentences.en: But her daughter, she's hardening herself at this point.
sentences.zh: 但她的女儿，此时此刻正在变得冷石心肠。

sentences.en: She says that, quite frankly, she just wants to move on from 80 Albert Street.
sentences.zh: 她说，坦白讲，她只想搬离阿尔伯特街80号。

sentences.en: I feel like all these people are relieved that what happened, happened because they were looking for a way out.
sentences.zh: 我觉得所有人对于发生的事其实都有种解脱感，因为他们一直在寻找出路。

sentences.en: You're looking at them and they're free and they're relieved deep down inside because it was hell.
sentences.zh: 你看着他们，他们自由了，内心深处感到释怀，因为这里简直是人间炼狱。

sentences.en: She doesn't want to have that memory.
sentences.zh: 她不想留下那段记忆。

sentences.en: You said that people clearly knew that a fire like this was possible, that these hijacked buildings, you know, are a phenomenon and that there are over 600 of them.
sentences.zh: 你说过，大家显然都知道可能会发生这样的火灾，你知道，这种被强占的大楼是一种普遍现象，而且有600多栋。

sentences.en: You called this inevitable in some ways.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你称这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: So who's at fault here?
sentences.zh: 那么，这究竟是谁的错？

sentences.en: You know, when I got to the scene, I asked the mayor that same question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我到达现场时，我问了市长同样的问题。

sentences.en: I said, people have been calling you about this building for years, to my records, at least since May.
sentences.zh: 我说，根据我的记录，多年来人们一直就这栋大楼给你打电话，至少从5月份就开始了。

sentences.en: So who is at fault here?
sentences.zh: 所以这到底是谁的错？

sentences.en: And he said, while his administration is new, everyone is at fault.
sentences.zh: 他说，虽然他的政府是新上任的，但每个人都有错。

sentences.en: And that is a catch all.
sentences.zh: 这是一个万能的借口。

sentences.en: Because that means that no one person will be held accountable here.
sentences.zh: 因为这意味着这里没有任何一个人需要承担责任。

sentences.en: Because what this building represents is a series of failures within the city and a series of failures within the country, quite frankly.
sentences.zh: 因为这栋大楼所代表的，说实话，是市政府的一系列失职，也是国家的一系列失职。

sentences.en: So my colleague, John Eligo, found a trove of documents that showed emails between city environmental officials sending emails to people in the health department, their colleagues
sentences.zh: 我的同事约翰·埃利戈（John Eligo）发现了一批文件，其中包含市环境官员发给卫生部门同事的电子邮件，以及他们在

sentences.en: in public safety, their colleagues in the Johannesburg Property Company, which was the state-owned entity that ran this company.
sentences.zh: 公共安全部门的同事，他们在约堡地产公司（Johannesburg Property Company）的同事，该公司是经营这家公司的国有实体。

sentences.en: And they said, we have had inspections here, at least from 2017.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们这里进行过检查，至少从2017年就开始了。

sentences.en: They listed all the problems with the building.
sentences.zh: 他们列出了这栋大楼的所有问题。

sentences.en: And they said that this is a bad building.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是一栋问题大楼。

sentences.en: It is turning into an emergency situation and we should do something about it.
sentences.zh: 它正在变成紧急情况，我们应该采取行动。

sentences.en: What we did not find is what exactly people did about it.
sentences.zh: 我们没有找到的是，人们到底对此做了什么。

sentences.en: But residents who live across the road, those are the people that I interviewed back in May already, said that they had also called the police.
sentences.zh: 但住在马路对面的居民——正是我早在5月份采访过的人——说他们也报过警。

sentences.en: They called the police when they heard screaMs.
sentences.zh: 当他们听到尖叫声时，他们报了警。

sentences.en: They called the police when they thought there was a murder, when they saw a woman being thrown off the third or fourth floor.
sentences.zh: 当他们认为发生了谋杀案、看到有女人被从三楼或四楼扔下来时，他们报了警。

sentences.en: And the police would come, there would be a raid, but then life would return to normal.
sentences.zh: 警察会来，会进行突击搜查，但随后生活又恢复正常。

sentences.en: And it would just go right back to the way things were.
sentences.zh: 一切又回到了老样子。

sentences.en: And so there are all these failures at every step.
sentences.zh: 所以在每一个环节都存在各种失职。

sentences.en: And when city officials were doing this sort of tour around the disaster, giving press conferences,
sentences.zh: 当市里的官员们在灾难现场进行某种视察、举行记者招待会、

sentences.en: giving press briefings, blaming each other, I asked one of the city officials, when was the last time you were inside this building?
sentences.zh: 发表新闻简报、互相推卸责任时，我问其中一位官员：你上一次进这栋楼是什么时候？

sentences.en: When was the last time there was an inspection?
sentences.zh: 上一次进行检查是什么时候？

sentences.en: And he said to me, it was in 2019 because we couldn't risk going into a hostile environment, a hostile environment where people lived.
sentences.zh: 他对我说，那是在2019年，因为我们不敢冒风险进入一个充满敌意、有人居住的敌对环境。

sentences.en: So stepping back for a minute here, Lindsay, you know, going back to something we talked about at the beginning of our conversation, Johannesburg as the symbol of hope and optimism
sentences.zh: 琳西，退一步讲，回到我们在对话开始时讨论过的一个话题，约内内斯堡曾是南非在1994年带给

sentences.en: that really all of us had about South Africa back in 1994.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人的希望和乐观的象征。

sentences.en: And now here we have this.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们却遇到了这种事。

sentences.en: And I mean, you know, I don't want to read too much into it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我不想过分解读。

sentences.en: We just had our own disastrous fire in the state of Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 我们自己在夏威夷州刚刚经历了一场灾难性的火灾。

sentences.en: But it does seem safe to say that this fire has shown Johannesburg to be a symbol of something else.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定地说，这场火灾表明，约翰内斯堡成了某种完全不同的象征。

sentences.en: What would you say it is?
sentences.zh: 你认为它代表了什么？

sentences.en: I think Johannesburg at this point is a symbol of the disappointment of what South Africa could have been.
sentences.zh: 我认为此时的约翰内斯堡象征着南非未竟之梦的破灭。

sentences.en: Johannesburg has all these precincts in which the city tried to build and create and make it safe and livable.
sentences.zh: 约翰内斯堡有这么多片区，市政府曾试图在那里建设、创造，使其变得安全宜居。

sentences.en: But even as I was driving here, I would see a developed building and next door was a hijacked building.
sentences.zh: 但即使在我开车来这里的路上，我也能看到一栋开发完好的大楼，而隔壁就是一栋被强占的大楼。

sentences.en: Every time there is one step forward, there are two to three steps back.
sentences.zh: 每次前进一步，就会倒退两到三步。

sentences.en: And to be sure, there are great gleaming stretches of the city that still show the old promise.
sentences.zh: 当然，这座城市确实有大片光鲜亮丽的地方，依然展现着昔日的希望。

sentences.en: But more and more for so many people, the city just doesn't hold the promise that it used to.
sentences.zh: 但对许多人来说，这座城市越来越无法承载昔日的希望了。

sentences.en: Lindsay, as someone from Johannesburg, whose life has spanned this period, how do you see it?
sentences.zh: 琳西，作为一名经历过这段时期的约翰内斯堡人，你是怎么看的？

sentences.en: You know, I grew up between a part of Soweto and Johannesburg suburbs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的成长足迹介于索韦托的一部分和约翰内斯堡郊区之间。

sentences.en: I was bused into school back and forth every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都坐校车往返于学校。

sentences.en: I've traveled from one end of Johannesburg.
sentences.zh: 我走遍了约翰内斯堡的各个角落。

sentences.en: And what I've loved about the city is its innovation, its diversity, its sense of energy.
sentences.zh: 我对这座城市的喜爱在于它的创新、它的多元、它的活力。

sentences.en: And what I am finding is that the spirit of the city is slowly waning and struggling.
sentences.zh: 而我现在的感受是，这座城市的精神正在慢慢消磨和挣扎。

sentences.en: The city is struggling to rise above this political disaster.
sentences.zh: 这座城市正在艰难地摆脱这场政治灾难。

sentences.en: It's struggling to rise above decades of neglect.
sentences.zh: 它在艰难地摆脱数十年的忽视。

sentences.en: And it's struggling to rise above what is becoming a national problem in South Africa, where it seems as if there is no clear path forward.
sentences.zh: 它在艰难地摆脱南非正在成为的一个全国性问题——在这里，似乎找不到一条清晰的前进道路。

sentences.en: And it seems as if the people who have been entrusted in steering the city and steering the country into this future that everybody dreamed about in 1994 are unable to do it.
sentences.zh: 似乎那些被委以重任、带领城市和国家走向1994年每个人都梦想的未来的领导者们，根本无力做到这一点。

sentences.en: And so, for the people that I have been talking to, what they're seeing this is, is a leaderless city.
sentences.zh: 因此，在与我交谈过的人看来，他们看到的是一个群龙无首的城市。

sentences.en: And that question is important because we are months away from a pivotal election.
sentences.zh: 这个问题之所以重要，是因为距离一场关键选举只剩几个月了。

sentences.en: Next year is not only the 30-year anniversary of democracy in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 明年不仅是南非民主30周年。

sentences.en: It's also an election year, where some pundits are saying that they believe that the ANC will go to its lowest margin yet.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个选举年，一些政治评论员表示，他们认为非国大（ANC）的支持率将创下历史新低。

sentences.en: It will still win.
sentences.zh: 它依然会赢。

sentences.en: But what we're seeing then is that likely that it will be at its weakeSt.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到的情况是，它很可能会处于最虚弱的状态。

sentences.en: And so, what we're questioning then is who steps into that gap.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在质疑的是，谁来填补这个空白。

sentences.en: And what I think is that the lesson here is rather than relying on a political party to
sentences.zh: 我认为这里的教训是，与其指望某个政党来

sentences.en: step into that gap, what I have seen in the days after the fire is South Africans and immigrant
sentences.zh: 填补这个空白，不如看看我在火灾发生后的日子里所看到的：南非人和移民

sentences.en: communities coming together to try and help each other, to feed each other, to find homes for each other, to help each other bury their dead.
sentences.zh: 社区团结在一起，试图互相帮助、互相喂饱、互相寻找住所、帮彼此安葬死者。

sentences.en: And so, what I hope is that South Africans will find their humanity in what has truly been an absolute tragedy.
sentences.zh: 因此，我希望南非人能在这场绝对的悲剧真正发生时，找回他们的人性。

sentences.en: And I hope that, unlike the previous times, that Johannesburg doesn't just move on from this one.
sentences.zh: 我希望，与以往不同的是，约翰内斯堡不要对这一次的灾难轻易翻篇。

sentences.en: Lindsay, thank you.
sentences.zh: 琳西，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”（Connections）游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基（Sam Mazursky）。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天制作“拼字蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母方框”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Thursday.
sentences.zh: 在周四。

sentences.en: Let me tell you something, New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 听我说，纽约人。

sentences.en: Never in my life have I had a problem that I did not see an ending to.
sentences.zh: 我一生中从未遇到过看不到尽头的问题。

sentences.en: I don't see an ending to this.
sentences.zh: 我看不到这件事的尽头。

sentences.en: New York Mayor Eric Adams escalated his rhetoric over the influx of migrants to the city, claiming in stark terms that the crisis was existential.
sentences.zh: 纽约市长埃里克·亚当斯（Eric Adams）就该市涌入的大批移民升级了措辞，严厉宣称这场危机事关生死存亡。

sentences.en: This issue will destroy New York City.
sentences.zh: 这个问题将毁掉纽约市。

sentences.en: Adams, a Democrat in his second year in office, has clashed with leading members of his party
sentences.zh: 作为一名上任第二年的民主党人，亚当斯与他党内的主要成员发生了冲突

sentences.en: as New York City has struggled to provide housing and services to the migrants, who now number 110,000.
sentences.zh: 因为纽约市一直在艰难地为目前已达11万的移民提供住房和援助。

sentences.en: For months, he has criticized President Biden and New York's Governor Kathy Hochul for failing to help the city.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，他一直批评总统拜登和纽约州长凯西·霍楚尔（Kathy Hochul）未能协助这座城市。

sentences.en: But his comments on Thursday were the most ominous yet and drew praise from Republicans and condemnation from some Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但他在周四的言论是迄今为止最不祥的，受到了共和党人的赞扬和一些民主党人的谴责。

sentences.en: And Peter Navarro, a trade advisor to former President Donald Trump, was convicted on Thursday of criminal contempt of Congress
sentences.zh: 前总统唐纳德·特朗普的贸易顾问彼得·纳瓦罗（Peter Navarro）周四被判藐视国会罪名成立

sentences.en: over his defiance of a subpoena from the House committee investigating the January 6th attack on the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 原因是他违抗了众议院调查1月6日国会山骚乱委员会的传票。

sentences.en: The verdict, in federal district court in Manhattan, made Mr. Navarro the second top advisor of Trump's to be found guilty of contempt for defying the committee's inquiry.
sentences.zh: 曼哈顿联邦地区法院的这项裁决使纳瓦罗先生成为特朗普的第二位因无视委员会调查而被判藐视法庭罪的高级顾问。

sentences.en: Stephen Bannon, a former strategist for Mr. Trump, was convicted of the same offense last summer.
sentences.zh: 特朗普先生的前战略师史蒂芬·班农（Stephen Bannon）去年夏天被判犯有同一罪行。
